Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned having blisters on your forearm and ulcers on your mucosal surfaces; can you tell me how long you have had these symptoms and if they are painful?

REQUEST TEST: Blood_CSF_Analysis, Skin_Biopsy
REQUEST IMAGES: Dermatology_Skin_Lesion, Oropharyngeal_Ulcer

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Blood_CSF_Analysis: Not requested in current dataset; Skin_Biopsy: Histopathology shows acantholysis and intraepidermal blister formation; Direct Immunofluorescence shows intercellular IgG and C3 deposition within the epidermis; Autoantibodies: Presence of desmoglein antibodies; CBC: Within normal limits.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Pemphigus Vulgaris. The findings of acantholysis, intercellular IgG/C3 deposition, and desmoglein antibodies are pathognomonic for this autoimmune blistering disease affecting the skin and mucosa.
